_about: Journeys page data (site/journeys.qmd). Edit this file, then run: python3 scripts/build_journeys.py (writes _journeys.qmd) and re-render.
Source of every fact: Henry's own account (2026-11-05) and his route images. Public text is English, one line per entry.
home: the place id of Henry's hometown (its province's tile says 'home' instead of a first-visit year).
chapters: one per place lived, in time order; colour = [day, night] (validated as a categorical set for adjacent chapters).

places: id -> name, admin (ISO 3166-2 style: CN-xx for China's provincial-level divisions, US-xx for U.S. states and DC), country (ISO alpha-2; HK for Hong Kong as a region), lat/lon (approximate city centres).

entries: date (YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD where the day is shown), optional end and when (the date words shown), chapter, text, places (the stops this entry claims: dots on the map), optional parent (a stop of a longer journey), transit (place ids landed at between flights) and noentry (transits without entering the country), first (list of 'first' badges), milestone (badge words), route or routes.

route: mode ground (by road or rail), flight, or unknown (way of travel not recorded); path = place ids and '@lat,lon' shaping points (shaping points make no claim of a visit; every mapped route is approximate); passes = provincial divisions or states passed through (they light the tiles); km = a distance Henry gave (otherwise the length of the drawn line is used).

summit (on a place): peak, m (elevation in metres, from the public source in src), tag; by (on a route or an entry): plane, train, car, bike or foot (the transport icons); by_draft: a note when the transport is assumed; title (on an entry): its short name in the almanac; hike (on an entry): place, dist (as Henry gave it, no added precision) and tag, shown as a hiking badge.
list: false keeps an entry off the chapter list (it still draws its dots and routes, counts, and shows in the map cards): the list records the journeys selectively (Henry, v4).
draft: a short note on what was inferred; on an entry, a place, or a pass (a code ending in '?'). Henry confirms or corrects these; the build lists them.
sources: Map data, loaded by the page: China, with its provinces, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macao and the South China Sea inset, from the China standard map as published with Apache ECharts 4.9.0 (Apache-2.0); other countries from Natural Earth (public domain) through world-atlas 2.0.2; U.S. states from the U.S. Census Bureau through us-atlas 3.0.1. Summit elevations from Wikipedia. Routes are drawn through approximate waypoints, not along the roads.

chapters.name: Baotou
chapters.line: A B.A. in English at Inner Mongolia University of Science and Technology, farther from home than I had ever been. Four years on the northern edge of the country, and the first journeys of my own, ending in a sixty-day loop around China.
chapters.draft: May the university be named on the site? Also: the chapter's end month (June 2014) is not stated; your text says you graduated in 2014 and started work in Shanghai in July.

chapters.name: Shanghai and Bali
chapters.line: A first job in Shanghai, and two months later a first posting abroad: thirteen months on Bali, at a power plant under construction. Away from the site, the island taught me to dive, to fly and to surf.

chapters.name: China, between postings
chapters.line: A year back in China between two postings abroad, with Shanghai as the base. It was also the start of a long road back to study.

chapters.name: Lagos
chapters.line: Two and a half years based in Lagos, working in West Africa. The way home ran through the Gulf and Istanbul, and its stops became places of their own; by the end, a part-time master's was complete and the next move was to study in America.

chapters.name: San Marcos
chapters.line: The first American home, a university town between Austin and San Antonio, and a second master's at Texas State University. The pandemic arrived halfway through, and the two years closed with six months in Washington, DC.

chapters.name: Dallas
chapters.line: The Ph.D. years at The University of Texas at Dallas, and the years the map of the United States began to fill in: long drives, first in company and then alone, from the deserts of West Texas to the Rocky Mountains. Conferences led farther, to Boston and to Europe.

chapters.name: Boston
chapters.line: A half-year internship in Boston, reached by driving across the South and up the East Coast. Autumn in New England followed, from Walden Pond to the coast of Maine.

chapters.name: Idaho Falls
chapters.line: Across the whole country by car to eastern Idaho, for an internship at Idaho National Laboratory. Yellowstone was a short drive away; the Ph.D. was defended that September, and the year ended with the long drive south.

chapters.name: Austin
chapters.line: A winter in Austin after the Ph.D.: commencement in Dallas in December, and in spring an offer from Kansas State University.

chapters.name: Manhattan
chapters.line: A postdoc at Kansas State University, in Manhattan, Kansas, at the edge of the Flint Hills. The log stays open.

entries.text: From home in Shouguang to university in Baotou: the farthest I had been.
Ordos and Hohhot: near enough to Baotou to become familiar ground.
Yinchuan, over the May Day holiday: a trip for its own sake.
Datong and Mount Heng, the northern of the Five Great Mountains.
first: First of the Five Great Mountains

entries.text: Qingdao, on the Yellow Sea, in the summer holiday.
By bicycle from Baotou across the Yellow River into the Kubuqi Desert.

Sixty days and 12,162 km around China: by train onto the Tibetan plateau, down through Yunnan, east to Guilin, north through Hunan to Mount Tai and around the Bohai; the Five Great Mountains finished, each climbed and descended on foot.

route.note: The line follows the 2013 route image leg by leg, in its colours and order; the named stops are yours, and the cities between them are read from the image's line (along the Yellow River, Tianshui, Changsha, Wuhan, Jinan, Weihai, Shenyang, Jinzhou, Qinhuangdao, Shijiazhuang and Taiyuan). Every province the line crosses is one of the caption's 17.

entries.title: Around China in 60 days

entries.text: Xi'an and Mount Hua, the West: the Qinling, the Terracotta Army, the Big Wild Goose Pagoda and Datang Everbright City.
Lanzhou, then Xining, Riyue Mountain and Qinghai Lake, with the rapeseed in flower.
By train onto the plateau, to Lhasa: the Jokhang Temple and Namtso.
Down into Yunnan: Shangri-La, Lijiang, Dali and Kunming.
East through Guizhou to the karst of Guilin and Yangshuo.
Into Hunan for Mount Heng, the South, and the old town of Fenghuang; then on through Hubei.
Henan: the Shaolin Temple below Mount Song, the Centre, and Kaifeng.
Mount Tai, the East: the last of the five.
Around the Bohai Sea and back through Shanxi to Baotou.
entries.draft: From the 2013 map: the provinces are named in its caption; the way around the Bohai (a ferry from Shandong to Liaoning) and the cities are read from its line. Your text calls the 2014–15 transit your first time in Beijing: was Beijing on this loop?

entries.text: Jinan, the capital of my home province.
Graduated with a B.A. in English.
Shanghai, and the first job.
Two summer months around Shanghai, Hangzhou and the water town of Wuzhen among them.
To Bali for the first project abroad, by way of a transit in Brunei that never left the airport.
Thirteen months on Bali, at a power plant under construction on the northwest coast; in the time off, nearly every corner of the island.
Under the water, in the air and on the waves: diving, with a scuba certification, paragliding and surfing.

Mount Huang, in Anhui.
A month in Nantong, across the Yangtze from Shanghai.

Doha, on the long way home.

Doha twice more, with time between flights to see the city.
Abuja, Nigeria's capital.
Beijing, at last with time to see it; then Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
Istanbul, where Europe meets Asia.

Left home in Shouguang for the United States, by way of Shanghai.
A day in Seoul between flights.

Austin, then a taxi to San Marcos and two years of study.

The pandemic begins.
NASA in Houston.
Six months living in Washington, DC.
Defended my master's at Texas State University.
To Dallas, to begin the Ph.D. at The University of Texas at Dallas.
A Thanksgiving loop through the desert: Carlsbad, White Sands, Guadalupe Mountains and Big Bend, home by San Antonio.

Thanksgiving again in West Texas and San Antonio, with a stop at Wonder World.
New Year's fireworks over Dallas.
Arkansas in May: a long day of hiking in Hot Springs National Park and an off-road drive, then Caddo Lake on the way back.
